newsitem.title: FRANCE: Staff at French teaching hospitals on strike.
newsitem.headline: Staff at French teaching hospitals on strike.

text.p: Staff went on strike at nearly all France's teaching hospitals on Wednesday in protest against government-decreed health curbs, but emergency services still operated.

A spokesman for the ISNIH hospital staff union said 22 of 26 university centres were affected by astrike which started on March 11, with the hospital in the Brittany capital Rennes joining the action.
Strikers plan to march through Paris from Bastille Square on Thursday, flanked by doctors in private practice hostile to the austerity reform.

On Tuesday Prime Minister Alain Juppe met 30 parliamentarians of the ruling centre-right coalition who will be sent across France to put the government's point of view across to hospital doctors and staff.

Juppe says that sweeping health care reforms, the main trigger of a crippling 24-day wave of strikes in late 1995, are vital partly to enable France to qualify for a planned single European currency from 1999.
The doctors say spending curbs will mean a rationing of France's universal health care. Doctors also say their pay does not match their long hours.
Public health care spending is the leading factor in France's welfare deficit, expected to show a shortfall of about 33 billion francs ($5.8 billion) in 1997 after 51.6 billion last year.
